stem: Read only the sentences about the Tessel Fault. Taken together, what do they tell you about it?
stimulus: Most faults beneath the Harlow Basin stay locked for decades and then release their stored strain all at once in a sudden earthquake. The Tessel Fault behaves differently. Instruments placed along it record steady movement of a few millimeters every year. In more than a century of record keeping, no large earthquake has been traced to it.
choices: It moves slowly and steadily instead of slipping in large sudden earthquakes.
It stays locked for decades and then slips all at once in one earthquake.
It is one of several faults that lie beneath the Harlow Basin region.
It is unable to produce an earthquake of any size, now or in the future.
explanation: Three sentences are about the Tessel Fault: it 'behaves differently' from the others, it moves a few millimeters every year, and no large earthquake has been traced to it. Put them together and you get a fault that creeps steadily and does not slip suddenly. This is the core move behind real questions that ask 'Which choice best describes...' or 'What does the text indicate about...' one named item: find every sentence about that item, including the one that sets it against its group, and combine them.

B.why: This describes the other faults in the basin, not the Tessel Fault. The text says the Tessel Fault 'behaves differently', so you gave the exception the group's behaviour.

C.why: This is true, but it describes something the Tessel Fault shares with every other fault in the basin. The question asks what the text tells you about this fault in particular, and the important point is how it differs.

D.why: The text says only that no large earthquake has been traced to the fault so far. It says nothing about small earthquakes or the future, so 'any size' and 'in the future' go further than the text does.

stem: Read only the sentences about the moon Pell. Taken together, what do they tell you about it?
stimulus: Nearly all of the moons circling the planet Ostra travel in the same direction that the planet spins, and they follow almost perfectly circular paths. Pell, one of the smallest of these moons, is the exception. It orbits Ostra in the opposite direction. Its path, however, is just as circular as those of its neighbors.
choices: It travels in the direction opposite Ostra's spin along a nearly circular path.
It travels in the same direction as Ostra's spin along a nearly circular path.
It travels in the same direction as Ostra's spin along a long, stretched path.
It travels opposite Ostra's spin because it was captured from somewhere else.
explanation: Two sentences describe Pell. One says it orbits in the opposite direction, and the other says its path is 'just as circular' as the others'. So Pell is an exception in direction only, not in shape. Real 'Which choice best describes...' questions often turn on exactly this: you have to know which feature makes the item an exception and which features it still shares with its group.

B.why: This describes the rest of Ostra's moons. The text calls Pell 'the exception' because it goes the opposite way, so you described the group instead of the exception.

C.why: This gets both features wrong. Pell's direction is what makes it unusual, and the text says its path is just as circular as the others'. You mixed up direction of orbit with shape of orbit.

D.why: The first half is correct, but the text never explains why Pell orbits backward. 'Captured from somewhere else' sounds scientific, yet no sentence in the text supports it. Read every choice all the way to the end.

stem: Read only the sentences about the Marrow Street Bridge. Taken together, what do they tell you about it?
stimulus: Most of the bridges in the old river district were built of timber, and all of them have long since been replaced. The Marrow Street Bridge, built of stone in 1840, still stands. Its heavy stone deck kept it in place through a century of floods. That same weight, however, is now too much for the softened riverbank to hold, and engineers have closed the bridge to traffic.
choices: Its heavy weight helped it survive floods but now makes it unsafe to use.
Its heavy weight helped it survive floods and still keeps it safe to use.
It was built of timber and, like the others, has since been replaced.
It is the oldest stone bridge still standing anywhere in the country.
explanation: One sentence says the heavy deck kept the bridge in place through floods. The next says 'that same weight' is now too much for the riverbank, so the bridge is closed. Combined, they tell you that one factor both protected the bridge and now endangers it. Real 'What does the text indicate about...' questions often want this kind of small combination of two sentences.

B.why: The first half is right, but the second half reverses the text, which says engineers have closed the bridge. You likely recognized 'helped it survive floods' and stopped reading.

C.why: This describes the other bridges in the district. The Marrow Street Bridge is stone, and it still stands, so you described the group instead of the exception.

D.why: The text compares the bridge only with the others in the river district and says nothing about the rest of the country. 'Oldest anywhere in the country' claims more than any sentence supports.

stem: Read only the sentences about the white-clay pieces. Taken together, what do they tell you about them?
stimulus: Most of the pottery recovered from the Rennick site was shaped from the dark clay that lines the nearby river. A handful of pieces, however, are made of a fine white clay. Geologists have found no deposits of that white clay anywhere within 200 kilometers of the site.
choices: They were made from clay that came from far away from the site.
They were made from the dark clay found along the nearby river.
They were made by merchants who traveled from a coastal city.
They make up the largest share of the pottery found at the site.
explanation: One sentence says these pieces are made of white clay. The next says no white clay exists within 200 kilometers of the site. Combine the two and the clay must have come from far away. Neither sentence says this by itself, which is why this kind of combining is the skill behind real 'Which choice best describes...' questions.

B.why: This describes most of the pottery at the site, not the white-clay pieces. 'However' marks those pieces as the exception, and you described the group instead.

C.why: The text shows the clay came from far away, but it never says who made the pieces or where they lived. Merchants and a coastal city are details you added, and no line supports them.

D.why: The text calls them 'a handful' and says 'most' of the pottery is dark river clay. You reversed which group is larger.
